caption: The 48 primary studies compared side by side, arranged by year of publication and, within a year, by first author
note: Note: Each row is a shortened version of the study’s record in the review’s extraction table. “Cross-generator tested?” says whether the detector was evaluated on generators that were absent from its training data; “Key limitation” mostly gives the weakness that the study’s own authors acknowledge; some cells carry a scope point noted by this review, for instance where the authors state no limitation.

rows.approach: Spectral forensics: power spectrum averaged azimuthally to 1D, then a classical classifier
rows.model: RBF-kernel SVM, logistic regression, unsupervised K-means
rows.dataset: Faces-HQ (authors' own, 40K), CelebA, FaceForensics++
rows.generators: Self-trained DCGAN, thispersondoesnotexist.com fakes, FF++ manipulations
rows.result: Faces-HQ: 100% accuracy from as few as 20 labelled examples; FF++ videos: 91% accuracy
rows.crossgen: No – each dataset tested alone
rows.limitation: Low-resolution content is harder to flag: much less of the frequency spectrum is available

rows.approach: Handcrafted PRNU-like fingerprint from averaged denoising residuals; the source is found by correlation
rows.model: Averaged denoising-filter residuals, no trained classifier
rows.dataset: Per source 1,000 RGB images (256x256); RAISE camera photos; category sets for CycleGAN / ProGAN / StarGAN
rows.generators: 9 CycleGAN configurations, 6 ProGAN, 5 StarGAN
rows.result: 90.3% source-attribution accuracy uncompressed; 90.1% at JPEG QF=95
rows.crossgen: No – known GANs only (source ID)
rows.limitation: Poorer for StarGAN male/smiling networks and real cameras (PRNU patterns of low energy)

rows.approach: Deep CNN applied to pixel co-occurrence matrices
rows.model: Deep CNN fed 3-channel co-occurrence matrices
rows.dataset: 56,000+ images in two GAN datasets (unpaired translation; facial attributes)
rows.generators: CycleGAN, StarGAN
rows.result: Over 99% accuracy on each dataset
rows.crossgen: Yes – train on one GAN, test on the other
rows.limitation: Just two GAN families tested; the abstract states no explicit limitation

rows.approach: Learns GAN fingerprints for fake detection and closed-set attribution
rows.model: Deep CNN attribution model; fingerprint drawn from its last 1x1x512 feature/weight tensors; AutoEncoder variant visualises it
rows.dataset: LSUN bedroom and CelebA (20,000 reals apiece); per source 100K train, 10K test
rows.generators: ProGAN, SNGAN, CramerGAN, MMDGAN (128x128x3 each)
rows.result: 5-class attribution (real + 4 GANs): CelebA 99.43%, LSUN 98.58%; 86.61 / 67.84 for a PRNU baseline
rows.crossgen: No – attributes only to known GANs
rows.limitation: Requires labelled samples from each possible source GAN; tested at 128x128 only

rows.approach: Spectrum classifier aimed at GAN upsampling artefacts; an AutoGAN simulator creates them, so no real fakes are needed
rows.model: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-34 on the log frequency spectrum, phase dropped
rows.dataset: 14-category CycleGAN image sets; AutoGAN trained on 4,000 MSCOCO images
rows.generators: CycleGAN mainly; StarGAN, GauGAN tested too
rows.result: AutoGAN-trained spectrum classifier, never shown a real fake: 97.2% mean leave-one-out accuracy
rows.crossgen: Yes – simulated artefacts expose unseen GANs
rows.limitation: Every classifier fails on GauGAN, which upsamples differently; hurt by upsampler mismatch

rows.approach: Classifies patches with restricted receptive fields; heatmaps locate the detectable patches
rows.model: Patch models from truncated Xception and ResNet (best: Xception blocks)
rows.dataset: CelebA-HQ (24,183) and FFHQ (60,000) for training; FaceForensics++
rows.generators: Glow, GMM face generator, ProGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2; FF++ manipulations
rows.result: Train ProGAN / test StyleGAN: AP 99.99; unseen resolutions: AP ~100
rows.crossgen: Yes – ProGAN-trained, scored on StyleGAN/Glow/GMM
rows.limitation: "No method is completely bulletproof": stronger generators, out-of-distribution inputs or adversarial attacks can beat it

rows.approach: Classical classifiers on a 1D azimuthal integral of the DFT power spectrum; spectral regularisation is also proposed
rows.model: SVM, logistic regression and unsupervised K-means on that spectral feature
rows.dataset: Faces-HQ (40K, authors' own), CelebA (202,599), FaceForensics++
rows.generators: CelebA: DCGAN, DRAGAN, LSGAN, WGAN-GP; FaceForensics++ deepfakes
rows.result: Faces-HQ 100% (SVM, 1000 samples); CelebA 100% (2000 samples); FF++ single frames 85%
rows.crossgen: No – (un)supervised tests within each dataset only
rows.limitation: Assumes generators that use up-convolution; with other synthesis methods these signatures may be absent

rows.approach: Analyses high-frequency Fourier spectral decay via fitted parameters
rows.model: KNN (k=5) using the fitted decay parameters
rows.dataset: ~5,000 FFHQ and Cat Head Detection dataset images; 10/90 train/test split
rows.generators: ALAE, PGGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, VQ-VAE2
rows.result: Mixed-generator training: 99.2% accuracy on 1024x1024 uncompressed images
rows.crossgen: No – none of the five generators held out
rows.limitation: 85% JPEG compression leaves generated and real spectra essentially indistinguishable; at 256x256, accuracy is 88.8%

rows.approach: DCT-spectrum analysis of grid-like artefacts left by upsampling, with simple classifiers
rows.model: On DCT spectra: a shallow CNN (4-conv-layer, ~170K params) and ridge regression
rows.dataset: LSUN bedrooms, FFHQ, CelebA
rows.generators: BigGAN, CramerGAN, MMDGAN, ProGAN, SN-DCGAN, StyleGAN
rows.result: FFHQ real-vs-fake: Ridge-Regression-DCT 100.00% (75.78% on raw pixels); CNN-DCT source ID: LSUN 99.64%, CelebA 99.07%
rows.crossgen: No – no experiment with a held-out GAN
rows.limitation: Purpose-built adversarial perturbations can still fool the classifier

rows.approach: Detects fake faces from global (Gram) texture statistics
rows.model: Gram-Net, a CNN built on global texture representations
rows.dataset: Reals: CelebA-HQ, FFHQ, CelebA; GAN face sets; natural: ImageNet / BigGAN
rows.generators: BigGAN, DCGAN, DRAGAN, PGGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN
rows.result: >98% in-domain; ~77.7% accuracy across GANs (StyleGAN train, DCGAN / DRAGAN / StarGAN test)
rows.crossgen: Yes – tested on unseen GAN models
rows.limitation: Studies texture contrast alone; real/fake differences are broader

rows.approach: Two-class real-vs-fake CNN; Blur+JPEG augmentation and careful pre- and post-processing
rows.model: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50
rows.dataset: ForenSynths: 720K ProGAN training images, LSUN reals, 11-generator test sets
rows.generators: Train: ProGAN; 11 test sets: BigGAN, CRN, CycleGAN, DeepFakes, GauGAN, IMLE, ProGAN, SAN, SITD, StarGAN, StyleGAN; StyleGAN2 tested separately
rows.result: Averaged across 11 test sets (ProGAN and 10 unseen generators): mAP 90.1 without augmentation, 90.8 with Blur+JPEG(0.5)
rows.crossgen: Yes – trained on ProGAN; 10 of the 11 test generators unseen
rows.limitation: Chance-level on traditional (Photoshop-style) edits; the authors hedge with "for now"

rows.approach: Counter-study of spectral-decay features: the upsampling choice can remove the high-frequency artefact
rows.model: KNN (k=5) over 3 spectral features, alongside SVM and MLP; GANs retrained with altered last-layer upsampling
rows.dataset: CelebA-HQ (512); CelebA (128) and LSUN Bedrooms (128)
rows.generators: DCGAN, LSGAN, StarGAN, WGAN-GP; supplementary: CRN, IMLE
rows.result: Detection rate drops to 0–0.3% under bilinear upsampling (baseline 84.8–99.8%)
rows.crossgen: No – one classifier per GAN
rows.limitation: Authors' own finding: CNN-generated images need not show high-frequency spectral decay, so detectors relying on it are unreliable

rows.approach: Contrastive learning on a network that limits sub-sampling
rows.model: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 without first-layer subsampling, plus 2 projection layers
rows.dataset: Train: 362K real LSUN + 362K ProGAN images; test: ImageNet, COCO, RAISE
rows.generators: Train: ProGAN; unseen test: BigGAN, CycleGAN, GauGAN, RelGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2
rows.result: Mean over unseen GAN architectures: 0.997 AUC, 95.6% accuracy
rows.crossgen: Yes – seven held-out GAN architectures
rows.limitation: Adversarial robustness deferred to future work

rows.approach: Critically evaluates leading GAN-image detectors on compressed, resized and unseen-generator images
rows.model: Xception, SRNet, Spec, M-Gb, Co-Net, Wang2020 ResNet50, PatchForensics (seven detectors) plus the authors' no-down variant
rows.dataset: Train: 362K LSUN real + 362K ProGAN fake; test: ImageNet, COCO, RAISE reals and ~39K synthetic
rows.generators: Train: ProGAN; test: BigGAN, CycleGAN, GauGAN, RelGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2
rows.result: On uncompressed unseen GANs several methods pass 0.9 AUC but drop sharply after compression or resizing; best no-down variant tops 90% accuracy
rows.crossgen: Yes – trained on ProGAN; 7 unseen GANs
rows.limitation: Authors note "we are still very far from having reliable tools for GAN image detection"; the robustness study is preliminary

rows.approach: ViT compared with a CNN classifier across forgery types
rows.model: EfficientNetV2-M vs ViT-Base
rows.dataset: ForgeryNet: 15 manipulation methods
rows.generators: GAN, reenactment and swap methods, e.g. ATVG-net, Deepfakes, FaceShifter, FS-GAN, StyleGAN2, Talking Head Video
rows.result: Trained on three face-transfer methods: EfficientNetV2-M 81.1% on one but 47.0% and 57.0% on the other two; ViT-Base ~62.0% on all three
rows.crossgen: Yes – subset training, testing on 15 methods
rows.limitation: Accuracy on new, unseen methods stays fairly low

rows.approach: Bilateral high-pass filtering (frequency and pixel level) to amplify frequency artefacts
rows.model: BiHPF front-end feeding a ResNet-50 classifier
rows.dataset: Real: LSUN, FFHQ; ProGAN images used in training
rows.generators: BigGAN, CycleGAN, ProGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2
rows.result: Trained on 4-class ProGAN: mean accuracy 84.2% and mean AP 81.8% across unseen GAN models
rows.crossgen: Yes – ProGAN-trained, tested on 5 unseen GANs
rows.limitation: None stated by the authors; only GAN generators are evaluated

rows.approach: FrePGAN: suppresses frequency artefacts using frequency-level perturbation maps
rows.model: ResNet-50 deepfake classifier plus a perturbation generator
rows.dataset: Train: ProGAN-generated images; test: FFHQ, LSUN, ImageNet, CelebA, COCO and Deepfake sets
rows.generators: BigGAN, CycleGAN, GauGAN, ProGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2
rows.result: Cross-model, 4-class training: 79.4% average accuracy and 87.2% average precision
rows.crossgen: Yes – seen and unseen GAN models
rows.limitation: Trade-off: frequency artefacts help detect known GANs but weaken cross-GAN generalisation

rows.approach: Attention fuses global spatial features with local patch features
rows.model: Two-branch ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 with a patch selection module and multi-head attention
rows.dataset: Diverse self-built test set: 19 generation models, 128,424 images
rows.generators: 19 models, e.g. BigGAN, Celeb-DF, CycleGAN, FF++, GauGAN, Pix2Pix, ProGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN/2/3, VAEGAN, WGAN
rows.result: Unseen models: 91.73% mean AP; mixed setting: 96.91% global AP
rows.crossgen: Yes – centred on unseen models
rows.limitation: Artefacts are harder to spot after high-resolution images are resized

rows.approach: Orthogonally trained CNNs, ensembled to favour real-image scores
rows.model: Five EfficientNet-B4 CNNs, ensembled
rows.dataset: Train: ~116K real (FFHQ, Metfaces, AFHQ2) + ~200K synthetic; test: StyleGAN3 pairs
rows.generators: FaceVid2Vid, score-based models, StarGAN-v2, StyleGAN2, Taming Transformers; unseen: StyleGAN3
rows.result: 0.9995 AUC over the global test set, unseen StyleGAN3 included
rows.crossgen: Yes – StyleGAN3 held out of training
rows.limitation: The CNNs' orthogonality is checked only empirically, without a theoretical basis

rows.approach: Interpretable detection using ViT-feature SVM support vectors as prototypes
rows.model: Fine-tuned ViT and SVM; repository adds xDNN, KNN, Naive Bayes
rows.dataset: Custom sets drawn from ImageNet, FFHQ, Oxford-IIIT Pet
rows.generators: Stable Diffusion and various other diffusion methods
rows.result: Within-dataset best (fine-tuned ViT + MLP head): Oxford-IIIT Pet 99.5%, image-to-image ImageNet 96.7%, class-conditional ImageNet 99.7%, FFHQ 99.4%; 93.0–97.2% with an SVM on fine-tuned features; 81.3% and 84.0% in cross-dataset tests
rows.crossgen: No – cross-dataset only; no generator held out
rows.limitation: Open datasets are scarce; evaluation on self-built custom datasets only

rows.approach: Analysis-only forensic study of spectral/frequency artefacts in synthetic images; no detector proposed
rows.model: None; power-spectrum, autocorrelation and radial/angular spectral analyses
rows.dataset: Real: ImageNet, FFHQ, LAION; fakes from 15 models
rows.generators: GANs: BigGAN, GALIP, StyleGAN-T, StyleGAN2/3; VQ models; DMs: ADM, DALL-E 2, eDiff-I, GLIDE, Score-SDE; latent DMs: LDM, SD, DiT
rows.result: None; artefacts characterised through spectral analyses, no detection metrics
rows.crossgen: No – no detector was trained
rows.limitation: Post-processing, the authors note, "may significantly modify and hide" these artefacts

rows.approach: Analyses forensic traces (spectral fingerprints) of diffusion models and evaluates existing detectors
rows.model: Spec, PatchForensics, Wang2020 (augmentation-trained ResNet-50), Grag2021 (first-layer downsampling removed)
rows.dataset: Real: COCO, ImageNet, UCID; fakes from COCO prompts
rows.generators: ADM, DALL-E 2, GLIDE, Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion; references: BigGAN, EG3D, ProGAN, StyleGAN2/3
rows.result: Averaged over 12 test generators (the training GAN and 5 diffusion models included): AUC ~75–93% and accuracy ~52–76% uncompressed; accuracy ~50–61% after resizing and compression
rows.crossgen: Yes – GAN-trained detectors run on diffusion images
rows.limitation: Generalisation is still the chief obstacle; GAN-trained detectors do badly on diffusion images, more so once compressed or resized

rows.approach: SeDID: per-step error between deterministic reverse steps and denoising diffusion steps
rows.model: Statistical variant SeDID_Stat and neural-network variant SeDID_NNs
rows.dataset: CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet and CelebA, each at 32x32
rows.generators: Only DDPM
rows.result: SeDID_NNs, mean over the three datasets: ACC 0.9399, AUC 0.9634
rows.crossgen: No – DDPM alone; other families absent
rows.limitation: Optimal timestep differs between datasets; odd trends on CelebA need more investigation

rows.approach: Real/fake classification by a nearest-neighbour or linear probe on frozen vision-language features; backbone not trained
rows.model: NN or linear probe on final-layer CLIP ViT-L/14 image features
rows.dataset: Train: 720k ProGAN real/fake images; test: ForenSynths, diffusion and autoregressive sets
rows.generators: BigGAN, CRN, CycleGAN, DALL-E, DeepFakes, GauGAN, Glide, Guided, IMLE, LDM, ProGAN, SAN, SITD, StarGAN, StyleGAN
rows.result: +15.07 mAP and +25.90% accuracy over prior best methods on diffusion and autoregressive models unseen in training
rows.crossgen: Yes – GAN-trained, evaluated on diffusion/AR
rows.limitation: Why frozen CLIP features tell real from fake images apart "remains an open question"

rows.approach: Large-scale dataset; multi-class classifier with reduced filter stride
rows.model: ConvNeXt-Large (altered stem)
rows.dataset: ArtiFact, 2,496,738 images in total: 964,989 real and 1,531,749 fake
rows.generators: 25 generation methods: 13 GANs, 7 diffusion models, 5 miscellaneous
rows.result: Tests 1–3 of IEEE VIP Cup 2022: accuracy 96.04%, 83.00% and 90.60% respectively
rows.crossgen: Yes – challenge tests use unseen generators
rows.limitation: Leading detectors still falter on generators unseen in training

rows.approach: Detects and attributes text-to-image fakes with image-only and hybrid (image plus prompt) classifiers
rows.model: Image-only: ResNet18; hybrid: CLIP image and text encoders plus a 2-layer MLP
rows.dataset: Real: MSCOCO, Flickr30k; fakes by four text-to-image models
rows.generators: DALL-E 2, GLIDE, Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion
rows.result: SD-trained hybrid detector (MSCOCO): accuracy 0.932 on Latent Diffusion, 0.899 on GLIDE, 0.885 on DALL-E 2
rows.crossgen: Yes – SD-trained, evaluated on three unseen T2I models
rows.limitation: Image-only detection on other models (e.g. GLIDE, DALL-E 2) is "far from the design goal"

rows.approach: LGrad (Learning on Gradients): pretrained-CNN gradients as a generalised representation of artefacts
rows.model: Pretrained-CNN transformation model mapping images to gradients, then a classifier
rows.dataset: ForenSynths / CNNDetection training data: 20 ProGAN categories, each 18,000 fake and 18,000 real; 1-, 2- or 4-class training
rows.generators: 8 test models: BigGAN, CycleGAN, Deepfake, GauGAN, ProGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2
rows.result: 1-class setting, mean across the 8 test models: 86.3% ACC, 92.7% AP; vs FrePGAN: +11.4% ACC, +13.4% AP
rows.crossgen: Yes – across models, data and unseen domains
rows.limitation: Authors' own framing: reliance shifts from the data to the transformation model

rows.approach: DIRE (diffusion reconstruction error): residual of an image versus its DDIM reconstruction
rows.model: ResNet-50 classifying DIRE maps; reconstruction by ADM (LSUN-Bedroom), 20 DDIM steps
rows.dataset: DiffusionForensics benchmark built on LSUN-Bedroom and ImageNet
rows.generators: Diffusion models (8): ADM, DDPM, iDDPM, LDM, PNDM, SD-v1, SD-v2, VQ-Diffusion
rows.result: ADM-trained detector: 99.9% mean accuracy, 100 AP over 8 diffusion models, unseen ones included
rows.crossgen: Yes – holds on unseen diffusion models
rows.limitation: None stated by the authors; covers only diffusion-generated images

rows.approach: Million-scale benchmark with tasks for cross-generator and degraded-image testing
rows.model: ResNet-50, DeiT-S, Swin-T, CNNSpot, Spec, F3Net, GramNet
rows.dataset: GenImage: >1M fake pairs and 1,331,167 real ImageNet images
rows.generators: ADM, BigGAN, GLIDE, Midjourney, SD v1.4, SD v1.5, VQDM, Wukong
rows.result: ResNet-50 accuracy: 99.9% on its training generator (SD v1.4), 54.9% on Midjourney
rows.crossgen: Yes – includes a cross-generator classification task
rows.limitation: Steep performance drops across generators and on low-resolution, JPEG-compressed or blurred images

rows.approach: Binary CNN real/fake classifier, explained via Grad-CAM
rows.model: Best of 36 custom CNNs: 2 conv layers of 32 filters, 64-unit dense layer
rows.dataset: 120,000-image CIFAKE dataset: 60k real (CIFAR-10), 60k synthetic
rows.generators: Stable Diffusion v1.4, a latent diffusion model
rows.result: Test accuracy of 92.98% on CIFAKE
rows.crossgen: No – SD v1.4 is the sole generator
rows.limitation: One generator at 32px; decisions hinge on background imperfections

rows.approach: Stable Diffusion inversion as detection features
rows.model: From-scratch ResNet50 on the image concatenated with its decoded noise map and reconstruction
rows.dataset: Real images: LAION, WebLI, reverse-image-search sets; SynRIS benchmark (new; 15 test sets)
rows.generators: Detector trained on SD; 15+ test models, e.g. DALL-E 2/3, Imagen, Kandinsky 2/3, Midjourney, PixArt-alpha, Playground 2.5, SDXL, Stable Cascade
rows.result: AUC-ROC 0.759 averaged over the tested generators (RIS protocol, SD+LAION training)
rows.crossgen: Yes – SD-trained; T2I models unseen in training
rows.limitation: Might not generalise beyond diffusion to text-to-image GANs or transformers; inversion costs significantly more compute

rows.approach: DRCT framework: contrastive learning on diffusion-rebuilt hard samples
rows.model: Backbones: ConvNeXt-B, CLIP-ViT-L/14 (UnivFD)
rows.dataset: DRCT-2M (the authors' million-scale set) and GenImage; MSCOCO reals
rows.generators: 16 diffusion model types, SD v1.4 and v2 included
rows.result: Accuracy rises by over 10% in cross-set tests (training on SD v1.4, testing on GenImage subsets)
rows.crossgen: Yes – cross-set tests on held-out diffusion models
rows.limitation: Smaller gains on non-diffusion (GAN) images; covers fully generated images only, not locally generated regions

rows.approach: Few-shot forensics: linear SVM over frozen CLIP features of a few reference images
rows.model: Linear SVM on penultimate-layer CLIP ViT-L/14 features
rows.dataset: Few-shot reference set: 10 to 10k paired real/fake images from one generator; 18-generator test suite
rows.generators: 18 in total: ADM, DALL-E 2/3, DeepFloyd-IF, DiT, eDiff-I, Firefly, GigaGAN, GLIDE, LDM, Midjourney v5, ProGAN, Score-SDE, SD variants, StyleGAN2/3/T
rows.result: ~90.0% mean AUC on the 18 generators; over the state of the art, +6% AUC out-of-distribution, +13% on impaired images
rows.crossgen: Yes – 18 test generators spanning 3 families
rows.limitation: Limited interpretability: it remains unclear which forensic cues CLIP relies on

rows.approach: Zero-shot, entropy-based: scores an image's coding cost with a model learnt only from real images
rows.model: ZED: multi-resolution, lossless neural image encoder
rows.dataset: Encoder trained on ~338k real images (Open Images); 19-generator synthetic test set
rows.generators: 19, among them ADM, BigGAN, DALL-E 1/2/3, DiT, Firefly, GauGAN, GigaGAN, GLIDE, Midjourney v5, SD/SDXL, StyleGAN2
rows.result: ~90.0% mean AUC on the 19 generators; average accuracy >3% above the state of the art
rows.crossgen: Yes – 19 never-seen generators, zero-shot
rows.limitation: Unreliable under heavy compression or resizing; catches only fully synthetic images, not local edits

rows.approach: Shows detection datasets carry JPEG-compression and image-size biases, and removes them
rows.model: Detectors: ResNet50, Swin-T
rows.dataset: GenImage
rows.generators: ADM, BigGAN, GLIDE, Midjourney, SD v1.4, SD v1.5, VQDM, Wukong
rows.result: Bias-corrected training lifts GenImage cross-generator accuracy by >11 pp: ResNet50 from 71.68% to 82.74%, Swin-T from 74.09% to 85.83%
rows.crossgen: Yes – across GenImage generator subsets
rows.limitation: Constraints notwithstanding, "datasets may contain other undesirable biases" such as style differences or generator fingerprints

rows.approach: Universal detection by prompt-tuning CLIP, a vision-language model
rows.model: Prompt-tuned CLIP ViT versus linear probe, fine-tuning and adapter
rows.dataset: Training: 200k ProGAN; testing: 21 datasets
rows.generators: GANs, diffusion models and commercial tools
rows.result: Prompt tuning: mAP 98.06%, mean accuracy 89.45% on 18 unseen generators
rows.crossgen: Yes – 21 test datasets, all unseen
rows.limitation: Weaker on images from commercial tools once JPEG-compressed

rows.approach: Uses intermediate CLIP encoder-block outputs, weighted by trainable importance scores
rows.model: RINE: small trainable projection/weighting network over intermediate blocks of a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14
rows.dataset: 1/2/4-class ProGAN training settings; 20 datasets for testing
rows.generators: BigGAN, CRN, CycleGAN, DALL-E, DeepFake, GauGAN, Glide (3), Guided, IMLE, LDM (3), ProGAN, SAN, SITD, StarGAN, StyleGAN/2
rows.result: 4-class training, 20 test sets: mean accuracy 91.5%, AP 98.8; +10.6% accuracy versus the state of the art
rows.crossgen: Yes – GANs and diffusion in 20 test sets
rows.limitation: Performance drops considerably when blur, crop, compression and noise are applied together

rows.approach: Forgery-aware CLIP adaptation: image- and frequency-domain adapter with language-guided alignment
rows.model: FatFormer: CLIP-ViT with forgery-aware adapter and text-prompt alignment
rows.dataset: Training: 4-class ProGAN; testing: unseen GAN and diffusion sets
rows.generators: Unseen test-time GANs and diffusion models
rows.result: Unseen GANs: 98% accuracy; unseen diffusion models: 95%
rows.crossgen: Yes – held-out GANs and diffusion models
rows.limitation: ProGAN-only training; authors note room to do better on diffusion models like Guided and call the GAN-diffusion artefact link unresolved

rows.approach: Diffusion-image detection with a LaRE (latent reconstruction error) feature
rows.model: LaRE feature with EGRE (Error-Guided feature REfinement module; spatial/channel align-then-refine)
rows.dataset: GenImage benchmark
rows.generators: GenImage's 8 generator subsets
rows.result: Surpasses prior best methods by up to 11.9% average ACC and 12.1% average AP over GenImage's 8 generators
rows.crossgen: Yes – evaluated on 8 GenImage generators
rows.limitation: Real/fake features still overlap for generators unseen in training (Midjourney, ADM, BigGAN); LaRE cannot stand alone as input

rows.approach: Training-free detection from an LDM autoencoder's reconstruction error
rows.model: Pretrained LDM autoencoders; LPIPS reconstruction distance; no classifier trained
rows.dataset: LAION-5B reals with prompt-matched fakes; Midjourney images from Discord
rows.generators: Stable Diffusion 1.1/1.5/2.1, Kandinsky 2.1, Midjourney 4/5/5.1
rows.result: Mean AP 0.992 over leading LDMs such as SD, Kandinsky, Midjourney
rows.crossgen: Yes – several LDMs, proprietary Midjourney included
rows.limitation: Best results need the source LDM's own autoencoder; limited to latent diffusion

rows.approach: Benchmarks GAN-image detectors on diffusion images, analyses frequency-domain artefacts, retrains them
rows.model: Wang2020 (ResNet-50); Gragnaniello2021; Mandelli2022 (an EfficientNet-B4 ensemble)
rows.dataset: Mainly LSUN Bedroom 256; also LSUN Cat/Horse, ImageNet, FFHQ
rows.generators: 5 GANs: Diff-ProjectedGAN, Diff-StyleGAN2, ProGAN, ProjectedGAN, StyleGAN; 5 DMs: ADM, DDPM, IDDPM, LDM, PNDM
rows.result: Average AUROC loss of 15.2% for GAN detectors on DM images; Pd@1%FAR averages 94.26% for a DM-trained detector on GANs but only 26.34% for a GAN-trained one on DMs
rows.crossgen: Yes – GAN-trained and DM-trained detectors cross-tested
rows.limitation: DMs leave fewer artefacts to detect; perturbations hurt DM-image detection more

rows.approach: Learning in frequency space: FFT-domain convolution on high-frequency image/feature representations
rows.model: FreqNet, a lightweight residual-block CNN (1.9M parameters, no pretraining)
rows.dataset: Train: ForenSynths ProGAN (1/2/4-class); test: GAN self-synthesis sets
rows.generators: 17 GANs, among them AttGAN, BigGAN, CycleGAN, GauGAN, ProGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN and StyleGAN2; also a Deepfake set
rows.result: Mean accuracy 92.8% on 17 GAN test sets, beating Ojha (83.0%) by +9.8%
rows.crossgen: Yes – ProGAN-trained, evaluated on 17 GAN sources
rows.limitation: The conclusion names no limitations; only GAN sources are evaluated

rows.approach: Up-sampling artefacts captured via Neighbouring Pixel Relationships (NPR)
rows.model: Lightweight CNN on NPR input; conv layers and ResNet blocks, 1.44M parameters
rows.dataset: ForenSynths ProGAN 4-class training split (car, cat, chair, horse); 18K real/18K fake each
rows.generators: 28 generators: 16 GANs, 11 diffusion models, 1 deepfake method
rows.result: Averages 92.2% accuracy on the 28 generators, +11.6% versus the previous best method
rows.crossgen: Yes – 28 held-out GAN and diffusion models
rows.limitation: None stated explicitly; training used only ProGAN 4-class data

rows.approach: Quantitative framework for scoring how XAI methods explain a deepfake detector
rows.model: Grad-CAM++, RISE, SHAP, LIME, SOBOL benchmarked on an EfficientNetV2 detector
rows.dataset: FaceForensics++
rows.generators: Four face manipulation methods: DeepFakes, Face2Face, FaceSwap, NeuralTextures
rows.result: LIME best: detector accuracy left at 0.579 on NeuralTextures after altering its top segment, 0.245 on DeepFakes after its top three
rows.crossgen: No – one detector, FF++ alone
rows.limitation: Explanation methods still struggle most with Face2Face and FaceSwap fakes

rows.approach: Supervised detector learnt from an extremely varied many-generator dataset
rows.model: CLIP-pretrained ViT-S classifier; ConvNeXt-S also trialled
rows.dataset: Training: Community Forensics (4,803 generators, 2.7M images); testing: Wang, Ojha, Synthbuster, GenImage, authors' 21-model set
rows.generators: 4,803 in total: latent/pixel diffusion, GANs, commercial systems
rows.result: On the out-of-distribution set of 21 unseen models: 0.987 mAP, 89.2% accuracy
rows.crossgen: Yes – 21 held-out models from 5 families
rows.limitation: Training data leans towards diffusion models; errors remain too frequent for critical uses

rows.approach: Injects a category-common prompt into CLIP's text encoder so that image features carry detection semantics
rows.model: C2P-CLIP: CLIP ViT-L/14 plus a category common prompt
rows.dataset: UniversalFakeDetect (train on ProGAN; 19 test subsets); GenImage (train on SD v1.4)
rows.generators: 20 in total: UniversalFakeDetect subsets plus GenImage diffusion models
rows.result: UniversalFakeDetect (19 test subsets): accuracy 93.79%, mAP 98.66%; GenImage: 95.8% accuracy
rows.crossgen: Yes – spans 20 generation models
rows.limitation: Prompt analysis by word frequency alone, without full captions, gives incomplete information

rows.approach: Mixture-of-experts fusion of frequency/noise (low-level) and semantic (high-level) cues; proposes Chameleon, an in-the-wild benchmark
rows.model: AIDE: SRM noise filters, a DCT scoring module and an OpenCLIP semantic encoder
rows.dataset: AIGCDetectBenchmark, GenImage, Chameleon (authors' own)
rows.generators: ADM, BigGAN, CycleGAN, DALLE-2/3, GauGAN, Glide, Midjourney, ProGAN, SD v1.4/1.5, StarGAN, StyleGAN/2, VQDM, Wukong
rows.result: Mean accuracy 92.77% (AIGCDetectBenchmark) and 86.88% (GenImage), but only 65.77% on Chameleon
rows.crossgen: Yes – 16+ generators, several benchmarks
rows.limitation: Every tested detector nearly fails on Chameleon's realistic images; the problem remains "far from being solved"

rows.approach: Effort: SVD splits frozen foundation-model features into orthogonal subspaces
rows.model: CLIP ViT-L/14 (ablations: BEiT-v2, SigLIP)
rows.dataset: Training: ProGAN; testing: 19 UniversalFakeDetect subsets, plus FF++ (deepfakes)
rows.generators: BigGAN, CycleGAN, DALL-E, GauGAN, GLIDE, Guided/Latent Diffusion, ProGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN
rows.result: mAP 99.41%, mAcc 95.19% over 19 test subsets, unseen generators among them
rows.crossgen: Yes – unseen generators among the 19 test subsets
rows.limitation: Authors raise only misuse risk and discuss no technical limitations
